decision: Reuse evidence and measurement practices; no framework installation, model calls, GPU search, kernel transplant or surrogate speed predictions justified by this audit

provenance.finding: giveen's NOTICE and CITATION explicitly identify an independent implementation. Its Rust search/performance extensions are not the paper authors' evaluated implementation.
The paper points to TorchedHat/KernelOPT; both webpage and GitHub API returned404 during this audit. Paper results must not be attributed to the independent giveen repository.

ForgeKernel's kernel index identifies a separate ForgeKernel paper under review on OpenReview. The README also links JustGoal arXiv2610.36434, a related but differently titled paper. OpenReview PDF was inaccessible through the web tool, so no claims of reviewing its full experimental protocol are made.

practical_workflow_findings.method: Measured-shape correctness and fresh final comparison
practical_workflow_findings.evidence: giveen's CUDA pipeline compiles/tests the selected source, then interleaves fresh baseline and candidate builds/benchmarks, records per-shape timings, and verifies correctness on the actually measured shape. Final performance verdict requires an effect beyond configured minimum and measured spread, all rounds won, and a bandwidth plausibility check.
practical_workflow_findings.critique: The loop always benchmarks baseline before candidate; its own testing guide recommends varying order. The noise variable used by the final verdict is the latest bench's recorded noise, not a derived confidence interval over paired ratios. All-round wins with few rounds are evidence, not statistical certainty. A generic 4x-DRAM ceiling is a diagnostic heuristic; cache residency and byte accounting must be checked. We cannot impose extra repetitions on the official fixed harness or spend unauthorized credits.

practical_workflow_findings.method: Bounded branch diversity with observed rewards
practical_workflow_findings.evidence: giveen's search filters to passed candidates, retains best-per-chain candidates and allocates expansions using an exploration heuristic based on measured latency and expansion count. It detects repetitive directions in recent plans.
practical_workflow_findings.critique: The score is 1/(1+latency_ms) plus c*sqrt(log(1+total)/log(1+expansions)); this is an implementation heuristic, not a calibrated performance model or standard finite-sample UCB guarantee. No fitted latency surrogate or held-out predictive validation was present in the inspected search implementation. Use it only as inspiration for an explicit experiment budget, not as a speed forecast.

practical_workflow_findings.method: Frozen-winner confirmation with node identity and per-workload rows
practical_workflow_findings.evidence: ForgeKernel's run_best_confirmation remeasures an exact source revision, keeps reference/candidate same-job ratios where available, records node identity and per-workload medians, warns when all samples came from one node, and labels incomplete confirmation provisional.
practical_workflow_findings.critique: Transfer source identity, ratio provenance and node accounting now. Do not copy automatic retries or repeated GPU confirmation under our exhausted local credit guard and bounded official quota. A separately measured median-versus-median fallback is weaker than a paired result.

practical_workflow_findings.method: Architecture contracts and evidence-backed knowledge records
practical_workflow_findings.evidence: ForgeKernel separates architectural decisions from later tuning, and stores hardware recipes with probe provenance. Its harvest guide explicitly says an agent-written probe only proves that mechanism ran, and human review still checks the knowledge claim.
practical_workflow_findings.critique: Our CPU proofs, compiler attributes, official correctness and measured speed must remain separate evidence fields. A valid schedule is not a performant schedule; a resource query is not achieved occupancy. Preserve failed mechanisms rather than silently promoting them into reusable truths.

practical_workflow_findings.evidence: ForgeKernel's self_evolve.py promotes only confirmed source with a gain above max(1.5%, observed same-job ratio spread); each new task preserves semantics and shape files with a copied reference.
practical_workflow_findings.critique: This spread threshold is a heuristic, not a confidence interval. Stopping when a search finds no further gain does not prove the hardware has no headroom, despite that wording in the script. Our existing frozen-incumbent policy already supplies most of the useful mechanism.

released_kernel_compatibility.kernel: ForgeKernel H100 gemm_fp16 (actual contract BF16 inputs/output, FP32 accumulation)
released_kernel_compatibility.observed: Persistent384-thread CTA, one128-thread producer warpgroup and two128-thread consumers, WGMMA shared/shared operands,128x256x64 tiles and four operand stages. Released code assigns producer/consumer register quotas40/232 with setmaxnreg. Its source ledger reports settled wait1 after comparing wait0/1/2; wait2 readings were mixed.
released_kernel_compatibility.relevance: Mechanism and lifecycle example only. Its dense8192-cubed campaign, shared/shared operands and large output accumulator differ from our small-token compressed-weight register/shared MoE and compressed dense projections. The source ledger's timing claims were not independently reproduced. It offers no reason to predict our WAIT2 gain.

released_kernel_compatibility.observed: SM100-specific FP8 E4M3 activations times E2M1 weights, UE8M0 power-of-two scale factors, block-scaled tensor operations and a large grouped campaign. Its preparation contract permits metadata/layout work different from our challenge rules.
released_kernel_compatibility.relevance: Reject direct transplant: H200 SM90 and BF16 activations with E4M3 NVFP4 scales require different hardware and arithmetic. Do not import its cached input-derived scheduling metadata or its precision contract into our submission.

released_kernel_compatibility.observed: Keeps running stage/phase counters across persistent tiles and calls for tests that actually wrap both work-tile and ring boundaries.
released_kernel_compatibility.relevance: Useful adversarial coverage principle already present in our WAIT2 and NW4 tests. No additional speed claim or new candidate follows from it.

next_actions: Resolve the already-submitted WAIT2 exact-source result before selecting another GPU experiment. Compare changed M32/M128/M256 and unchanged M1/M8/M16, plus compiler/resource evidence, using the predefined gate.

Review the sibling's320-schedule CPU pruner as a correctness/resource-feasibility manifest only. Keep unmeasured physical registers, local memory, actual occupancy and speed explicitly UNKNOWN; do not rank legal schedules by predicted speed without validated measurements.

If WAIT2 exposes register pressure or forced serialization, consider a CPU-only feasibility plan for full-warpgroup producer/consumer register redistribution. Current WGS has512 compute plus64 producer threads and no setmaxnreg. NVIDIA requires all warps in a warpgroup to execute the same setmaxnreg; a naive two-warp producer decrease is invalid. A640-thread design with a full128-thread producer group would be a separate architecture, with barrier/role/launch/PDL and actual-resource proofs before any candidate.

Do not fit a latency surrogate to our handful of heterogeneous structural failures. First define stable features, same-workload paired targets, missing-resource values, and a held-out mechanism or shape evaluation; until those exist, analytical pruning and measured final gates are the defensible tools.
